new_candidates.body:
### Bug Description

With `requires_grad=False`, a scene with a single `MPM.Sand` entity crashes on the first `scene.step()` with a CUDA illegal memory access once particle count × grid size × substeps is large enough. On an RTX 5070 Ti: 1.45 M particles, `grid_density=24` on an 11 × 12 × 5.7 m domain and `substeps=10` crash; the same scene with `substeps=2`, with a 7× smaller grid, or with 1.3 M particles runs fine. VRAM use is ~2 GB, so it is not an allocation problem. The same run passes under `compute-sanitizer` and with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, i.e. it is a race.

Cause: in `MPMSolver.substep_post_coupling` the sparse-reset counter is cleared through a zero-copy torch view (`qd_to_torch(self.grid_dirty_count, copy=False).zero_()`). That memset runs on torch's CUDA stream, unsynchronised with the Quadrants kernels. When it lands after the next `p2g` has started appending, the dirty entries of consecutive substeps accumulate until `grid_dirty_list` overflows (`self.grid_dirty_list[slot_idx] = flat` writes out of bounds). Introduced in #2720. A fix (clear the counter with a Quadrants kernel so it is stream-ordered) follows as a PR.

### Steps to Reproduce

```python
import genesis as gs

gs.init(backend=gs.gpu)
scene = gs.Scene(
    sim_options=gs.options.SimOptions(dt=4e-3, substeps=10),
    mpm_options=gs.options.MPMOptions(lower_bound=(-1, -7.5, -0.2), upper_bound=(10, 4.5, 5.5), grid_density=24),
    show_viewer=False,
)
scene.add_entity(gs.morphs.Plane())
sand = scene.add_entity(material=gs.materials.MPM.Sand(), morph=gs.morphs.Box(pos=(4.5, -1.5, 1.6), size=(3.0, 3.0, 3.0)))
scene.build()  # ~1.45M particles
for _ in range(5):
    scene.step()  # illegal memory access on the first step
```

Passes with `substeps=2`, with `size=(2.8, 2.8, 2.8)` (1.3 M particles), or with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`.

### Expected Behavior

The step completes; the number of particles should only be limited by memory.

### Screenshots/Videos

_No response_

### Relevant log output

```shell
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
Search for `cudaErrorIllegalAddress' in https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html for more information.
[Genesis] [ERROR] AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
[E ...] [cuda_driver.h:operator()@94] CUDA Error CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS: an illegal memory access was encountered while calling stream_synchronize (cuStreamSynchronize)
```

### Environment

- OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS
- GPU/CPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti (16 GB)
- GPU-driver version: 595.84
- CUDA / CUDA-toolkit version: 12.8 (torch 2.11.0+cu128), Quadrants 1.0.2

### Release version or Commit ID

main, 9f0fa583 (also reproduced on 573ccdf5)
new_candidates.title: [Bug]: MPM: CUDA illegal memory access above ~1M particles (race in the sparse grid reset)

new_candidates.body:
### Summary

Consider a model where many box geoms are grouped into static (dof-less) child bodies of the world. Since 3.8.0 it spends about 2.4× more time in the broadphase (`mjTIMER_COL_BROAD`) than in 3.7.0, and 3.17.0 adds another 1.37×. The same geoms, at the same absolute positions, placed directly in the world body cost about 16 µs per step in every release from 3.3.7 to 3.17.0.

### Reproduction

The script below (`static_bodies_broadphase.py`) builds a synthetic model:
- a ground plane;
- a free box resting on the plane;
- 100 × 200 small static boxes on a grid (20,002 geoms in total).

`--layout bodies` groups the boxes into 100 static child bodies of the world. `--layout world` puts the same boxes directly in the world body. The script steps the model 2000 times and prints:
- the median `mj_step` time;
- the per-step `mjTIMER_COL_BROAD` duration, recorded with `mjcb_time`.

```
pip install mujoco==<version> numpy
python static_bodies_broadphase.py --layout bodies
python static_bodies_broadphase.py --layout world
```

<details>
<summary>static_bodies_broadphase.py</summary>

```python
"""Broadphase cost of many box geoms held by static (dof-less) child bodies of the world.

Builds a synthetic model: a ground plane, a free-floating box resting on it, and
`bodies` x `geoms` small static boxes laid out on a grid. With --layout bodies the boxes
are grouped into `bodies` static child bodies of the world; with --layout world the same
boxes, at the same absolute positions, are direct children of the world body. Prints the
median mj_step time and the per-step broadphase timer (mjTIMER_COL_BROAD).

Usage: python static_bodies_broadphase.py [--bodies 100] [--geoms 200] [--layout bodies|world]
"""

import argparse
import json
import math
import time

import mujoco
import numpy as np


def model_xml(bodies: int, geoms: int, layout: str) -> str:
    side = math.ceil(math.sqrt(geoms))
    tiles = math.ceil(math.sqrt(bodies))
    pitch, tile = 0.2, 0.2 * side + 1.0
    parts = []
    for b in range(bodies):
        ox, oy = (b % tiles) * tile + 2.0, (b // tiles) * tile + 2.0
        boxes = []
        for g in range(geoms):
            x, y = (g % side) * pitch, (g // side) * pitch
            if layout == "world":
                x, y = x + ox, y + oy
            boxes.append(f'<geom type="box" size="0.05 0.05 0.5" pos="{x:.3f} {y:.3f} 0.5"/>')
        if layout == "world":
            parts.extend(boxes)
        else:
            parts.append(f'<body pos="{ox:.3f} {oy:.3f} 0">{"".join(boxes)}</body>')
    return f"""<mujoco>
  <option timestep="0.002"/>
  <worldbody>
    <geom name="floor" type="plane" size="0 0 0.1"/>
    {"".join(parts)}
    <body name="mover" pos="0 0 0.2">
      <freejoint/>
      <geom type="box" size="0.2 0.1 0.05" mass="1"/>
    </body>
  </worldbody>
</mujoco>"""


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--bodies", type=int, default=100)
    parser.add_argument("--geoms", type=int, default=200)
    parser.add_argument("--layout", choices=["bodies", "world"], default="bodies")
    parser.add_argument("--steps", type=int, default=2000)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    model = mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_string(model_xml(args.bodies, args.geoms, args.layout))
    data = mujoco.MjData(model)
    for _ in range(200):
        mujoco.mj_step(model, data)
    mujoco.set_mjcb_time(time.perf_counter)
    for timer in data.timer:
        timer.duration, timer.number = 0, 0
    samples = []
    for _ in range(args.steps):
        start = time.perf_counter_ns()
        mujoco.mj_step(model, data)
        samples.append(time.perf_counter_ns() - start)
    mujoco.set_mjcb_time(None)
    broad = data.timer[int(mujoco.mjtTimer.mjTIMER_COL_BROAD)].duration / args.steps
    print(json.dumps({
        "mujoco": mujoco.__version__,
        "layout": args.layout,
        "nbody": int(model.nbody),
        "ngeom": int(model.ngeom),
        "ncon": int(data.ncon),
        "stepMedianUs": round(float(np.median(samples)) / 1000, 1),
        "broadphaseUs": round(broad * 1e6, 1),
    }))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

### Results

Each cell is the median of 3 runs, in µs per step. Linux x86_64, Python 3.11.15, numpy 2.3.3, one process pinned to one core. Both layouts have the same `ncon` (4).

| mujoco | static child bodies: `mj_step` | static child bodies: broadphase | world body: `mj_step` | world body: broadphase |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3.3.7 | 261.7 | 148.7 | 126.8 | 16.1 |
| 3.4.0 | 246.2 | 124.1 | 134.8 | 16.0 |
| 3.5.0 | 236.7 | 130.2 | 124.6 | 16.1 |
| 3.6.0 | 236.4 | 124.9 | 124.6 | 16.3 |
| 3.7.0 | 236.5 | 125.9 | 124.8 | 16.7 |
| **3.8.0** | **425.4** | **302.3** | 124.2 | 16.2 |
| 3.9.0 | 429.2 | 306.4 | 124.7 | 16.4 |
| 3.10.0 | 425.4 | 303.2 | 125.3 | 16.5 |
| 3.11.0 | 427.5 | 305.1 | 125.4 | 16.5 |
| 3.12.0 | 425.4 | 304.5 | 124.5 | 16.7 |
| 3.13.0 | 425.6 | 302.8 | 123.6 | 16.0 |
| 3.14.0 | 425.9 | 304.6 | 124.8 | 15.9 |
| 3.15.0 | 422.4 | 302.5 | 124.2 | 16.1 |
| 3.16.0 | 424.8 | 302.4 | 124.5 | 16.0 |
| **3.17.0** | **539.5** | **416.6** | 124.3 | 16.2 |

All other pipeline stages are unchanged in our measurements: narrowphase, kinematics and the constraint solve. The slowdown is entirely in `mjTIMER_COL_BROAD`.

In a larger real model (about 22,000 static boxes in about 110 static child bodies, plus an articulated robot), the broadphase rose from 190 µs per step on 3.3.7 to 486 µs on 3.17.0. That made a 500 Hz real-time loop miss its deadlines.

### Workaround

Moving the static geoms into the world body brings the broadphase back to about 16 µs in every release; positions are made absolute, and nothing else changes. Compiling with `fusestatic="true"` has the same effect, but it also fuses the welded bodies of articulated models, which is not always acceptable.

### Expected

Geoms in static child bodies (`body_weldid == 0`) should cost about the same in the broadphase as geoms in the world body, as they did up to 3.7.0. At the least, the cost should not grow with each release.

We did not bisect individual commits. The first slow release is 3.8.0, and 3.17.0 adds a second step.
new_candidates.title: Broadphase cost of geoms in static child bodies regressed in 3.8.0 and again in 3.17.0
